messages:
Hannah: Quick Q for folks traveling internationally next week  SIM card vs eSIM vs pocket WiFi? What do you actually use?
Leo: eSIM for short trips if my phone supports it. No fiddling with trays at the airport.
Priyanka: I do eSIM + physical SIM when I know I'll be roaming a lot. Also works as a backup.
Grant: Pocket WiFi if we're a small team and want a single hotspot for laptops. Battery life can be meh though.
Hannah: Anyone had bad luck with eSIM activation while changing carriers? Worried about losing service mid-journey.
Leo: Once had to reboot and reapply the eSIM profile at the gate. Took 10 mins but worked. Keep a screenshot of the QR and provider email handy.
Priyanka: Pro tip: buy a local physical SIM on arrival for long stays. Cheaper than data plans and better coverage.
Grant: If you're doing a multi-country trip EU/Schengen-wise, a single pocket WiFi or an EU SIM is easier than juggling eSIMs.
Hannah: Poll: eSIM / physical SIM on arrival / pocket WiFi / dual strategy  react with emoji
Leo: ":iphone:" for eSIM
Priyanka: ":sim_card:" for physical SIM
Grant: ":satellite:" for pocket WiFi
Hannah: ":two_hearts:" for dual strategy
travel-bot: Note: Some countries block certain tethering services. Check local regs before buying pocket WiFi. Also keep roaming receipts for expense reports if reimbursing. :robot_face:
Priyanka: Also download offline maps (Maps.me or Google offline areas) and a few downloadable podcasts. Saved me when the pocket WiFi died.
Leo: Bring a short USB-C OTG SIM eject pin or paperclip. Tiny thing but a lifesaver when your phone cover hides the tray.
Grant: Meme: "me: buys global data plan" 
"also me: spends 3 hours swapping SIMs at midnight in a foreign airport" (image)
Hannah: OK looks like I'll do dual strategy. Thanks! If anyone has spare local SIMs from previous trips I'm happy to borrow for testing.
Priyanka: I have an old EU SIM I can leave at the front desk. Ping me.
Leo: Safe travels  and back up your phone before fiddling with SIM profiles.
Hannah: @here tiny reminder: plug adapters and a small power bank make the difference if you're relying on pocket WiFi. See you at the offsite!
